ro.root.designSystem.title: The shared visual foundation for the website and client portal.
ro.root.designSystem.intro: This page renders every token, primitive and state defined in docs/design/design-system.md and docs/design/patterns.md. It is the reference during development. It is intentionally not linked from production navigation.
ro.root.designSystem.colors.title: A small palette, used with intent.
ro.root.designSystem.colors.intro: Brand green is for actions and meaningful highlights only — never decoration. Green backgrounds always carry dark text; green text only appears on dark surfaces.
ro.root.designSystem.type.title: JetBrains Mono, tuned like an editorial type system.
ro.root.designSystem.type.intro: Headlines set tight and large; labels set small, uppercase and tracked. Body copy never goes below 14px.
ro.root.designSystem.components.title: Restrained primitives, aligned to the reference.
ro.root.designSystem.components.intro: Buttons, badges, cards and links. One radius family, 1px borders, and no decoration beyond what the approved designs use.
ro.root.designSystem.states.title: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
ro.root.designSystem.states.intro: No color inventions. Skeleton uses the line tone, empty states a dashed border, errors stay on the paper surface with strong dark emphasis.
ro.root.designSystem.states.loading: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
ro.root.designSystem.states.whenProjectExis: When a project or request exists, it will appear here.
ro.root.designSystem.states.tryAgain: Try again, or contact support if the problem persists.
ro.root.designSystem.darkSurface.title: Dark sections carry the same system.
ro.root.designSystem.darkSurface.intro: Primary text turns light, secondary turns fog, and green is used for highlights. Border line darkens to keep the composition quiet.
ro.root.designSystem.brandSurface.title: One brand section per page, at most.
ro.root.designSystem.brandSurface.intro: Green backgrounds carry dark text. Use this sparingly — it is the loudest surface in the system.
ro.root.enquiry.title: Start a project
ro.root.enquiry.subtitle: Tell us what you are trying to build, modernize, automate or fix. A useful enquiry starts with the pressure on the system and the decision you need to make.
ro.root.enquiry.body: The form collects the minimum information needed to respond thoughtfully. Nothing is shared outside SDK Enterprises, and you can also reach us directly at hello@sdk.enterprises.
ro.root.enquiry.body2: Your technical and commercial context stays together while SDK assesses whether the work is a fit.
ro.root.enquiry.heroSignals[0]: A finished specification is not required
ro.root.enquiry.heroSignals[1]: Technical and commercial context stays together
ro.root.enquiry.reasonsHeading: Bring the pressure on the system, not a polished procurement document.
ro.root.enquiry.reasonsIntro: The form is designed to establish whether SDK can make the next technical decision easier.
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[0].title: A system needs to change
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[0].copy: Modernization, migration or integration work is blocked by uncertainty in the current state.
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[1].title: A platform is under pressure
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[1].copy: Reliability, delivery speed, infrastructure or data behavior has become a business constraint.
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[2].title: An AI workflow needs engineering controls
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[2].copy: The use case is promising, but data, evaluation, review or operation is not yet defined.
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[3].title: A workstream needs the right specialists
ro.root.enquiry.reasons[3].copy: The outcome is clear, but the project crosses disciplines the current team cannot cover alone.
ro.root.enquiry.formHeading: Give us enough information to respond usefully.
ro.root.enquiry.formIntro: Explain what is happening, why it matters and what has already been tried. Unknown budget, timing or technical details can remain marked as such.
ro.root.enquiry.nextStepsBody: After you submit the form, we read it ourselves. If it is a fit, we will reply with a short written assessment and a proposed engagement model. If it is not a fit, we will tell you why and suggest an alternative.
ro.root.enquiry.nextStep1Body: We review the system, constraint and requested outcome against SDK's current capacity and relevant expertise.
ro.root.enquiry.nextStep2Body: A short written response: what we think the problem is, whether it is a fit, and what the first move would be.
ro.root.enquiry.nextStep3Body: A 30-minute call or an async exchange to clarify scope, constraints, and timeline. No pitch deck unless you want one.
ro.root.enquiry.nextStep4Body: A written proposal with scope, fixed price or rate, timeline, and milestones. You sign, we start.
ro.root.enquiry.validation.descriptionTooSh: Description must be at least 50 characters
ro.root.enquiry.validation.contextTooLong: Supporting context must be under 4000 characters
ro.root.enquiry.success.title: Enquiry sent
ro.root.enquiry.success.body: Thanks — we'll review the project context and reply with the next useful question or an assessment of fit.
ro.root.enquiry.error.title: Something went wrong
ro.root.enquiry.error.body: We couldn't send your enquiry. Please try again or email us directly.
ro.root.homePage.hero.eyebrow: Software · AI · Cloud · Data · Systems Engineering
ro.root.homePage.hero.title: Bring the system that needs a responsible way forward.
ro.root.homePage.hero.intro: SDK Enterprises assembles the engineering specialists a project actually requires, coordinates their work and remains accountable for the quality framework presented to the client. We help organizations diagnose, modernize, build and operate technically consequential software.
ro.root.homePage.opening.heading: A technology list cannot tell you what the project needs.
ro.root.homePage.opening.body: A modernization programme, an AI workflow and a platform reliability problem may touch similar technologies while requiring completely different decisions, disciplines and delivery controls. SDK starts with the pressure on the system and the outcome the organization needs to own.
ro.root.homePage.opening.body2: That may lead to a bounded technical assessment, a focused engineering workstream or a continuing technical partnership. The commitment should match what is already known—not conceal uncertainty inside a larger proposal.
ro.root.homePage.opening.principles[0].copy: When the current state or implementation path is unclear, establish the evidence needed for a responsible decision first.
ro.root.homePage.opening.principles[1].copy: Select the disciplines the system requires instead of forcing every engagement into the same available team.
ro.root.homePage.opening.principles[2].copy: Keep decisions, repositories, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge under client control.
ro.root.homePage.system.heading: The work rarely stops at the boundary of one technology.
ro.root.homePage.system.intro: SDK can focus on one layer or coordinate a workstream that crosses several. The map below shows the engineering concerns that often need to be considered together.
ro.root.homePage.system.items[0].title: Workflow and interface
ro.root.homePage.system.items[0].copy: The user task, operational decision and recovery path the software must make understandable.
ro.root.homePage.system.items[1].title: Business platform
ro.root.homePage.system.items[1].copy: The services, APIs, permissions and integration contracts that carry the organization’s rules.
ro.root.homePage.system.items[2].title: AI and automation
ro.root.homePage.system.items[2].copy: The model-assisted decisions, retrieval, evaluation and human review controls inside a real workflow.
ro.root.homePage.system.items[3].title: Data and state
ro.root.homePage.system.items[3].copy: The ownership, consistency, search, cache and lifecycle rules behind system behavior.
ro.root.homePage.system.items[4].title: Production operation
ro.root.homePage.system.items[4].copy: The deployment, observability, recovery and infrastructure mechanisms needed to operate the system.
ro.root.homePage.scenarios.heading: Technical work becomes urgent through its effect on the business.
ro.root.homePage.scenarios.intro: The following scenarios are capability examples, not invented client case studies. They show how SDK connects symptoms to questions and tangible next deliverables.
ro.root.homePage.companyModel.heading: A project-specific team without transferring coordination risk to the client.
ro.root.homePage.companyModel.intro: SDK works with independent engineering specialists. The disciplines can change with the work, while the client retains one company relationship and one delivery framework.
ro.root.homePage.engagements.eyebrow: Choose the right level of commitment
ro.root.homePage.engagements.heading: Do not buy implementation before the system can support an implementation decision.
ro.root.homePage.engagements.intro: Start with evidence when uncertainty is material. Move directly into delivery when the outcome, boundary and acceptance conditions are already understood.
ro.root.homePage.process.heading: Every stage should end with evidence and a decision.
ro.root.homePage.process.intro: Activity alone does not show that a project is progressing. SDK structures the engagement so the client can review what has been learned, built and transferred before making the next commitment.
ro.root.homePage.quality.heading: Confidence should come from visible mechanisms, not adjectives.
ro.root.homePage.quality.intro: Terms such as secure, scalable and production-ready only become meaningful when the engagement defines how they will be examined for the actual system and risk.
ro.root.homePage.fit.heading: The engagement needs a real constraint, system access and someone able to decide.
ro.root.homePage.fit.intro: SDK is designed for owned technical outcomes. It is not a marketplace for anonymous ticket capacity or a way to validate a predetermined answer without examining the evidence.
ro.root.homePage.cta.title: You do not need to turn the problem into a polished specification first.
ro.root.homePage.cta.body: Tell us what the system is doing, what it is costing or delaying, and which decision is currently blocked. SDK will begin by determining whether the work is a fit and what the first useful move should be.
ro.root.homePage.cta.label: Discuss the situation

ro.root.aboutPage.hero.title: A company built to compose the right engineering capability for the work.
ro.root.aboutPage.hero.intro: SDK engages independent engineering specialists according to the system and remains responsible for the delivery framework and quality expectations presented to the client.
ro.root.aboutPage.model.heading: The available bench does not decide what your system receives.
ro.root.aboutPage.model.intro: A fixed internal team can be efficient when every project needs the same disciplines. Complex systems often do not. SDK starts with the problem, determines which engineering capability is relevant and brings the required independent specialists into one engagement.
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[0].title: One client relationship
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[0].copy: The client engages SDK Enterprises. SDK provides the delivery framework instead of leaving the client to coordinate unrelated individual suppliers.
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[1].title: A composed team
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[1].copy: The disciplines involved can change with the stage of work, from assessment and architecture to implementation and operation.
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[2].title: Shared quality expectations
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[2].copy: The engagement defines review practices, acceptance evidence, decision records and handover requirements appropriate to its risks.
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[3].title: Client control
ro.root.aboutPage.model.items[3].copy: Repositories, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge are organized to remain under the client’s control.
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.heading: Relevant experience matters more than adding another profile to the project.
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.body: SDK considers the system, delivery stage, technical risk and collaboration needs before composing a team. The public site will not claim a network size, acceptance rate or universal seniority standard without a documented basis.
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[0].title: Problem relevance
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[0].copy: Experience is considered against the actual system boundary and technical decisions, not only a list of technologies.
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[1].title: Delivery responsibility
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[1].copy: Specialists need to work within visible decisions, review expectations and client-owned environments.
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[2].title: Collaboration fit
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[2].copy: The ability to explain trade-offs and work with client stakeholders is part of successful technical delivery.
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[3].title: Continuity
ro.root.aboutPage.selection.items[3].copy: Important context is recorded so ownership does not depend on one contributor remaining indefinitely.
ro.root.aboutPage.responsibility.heading: Flexible team composition should not create ambiguous accountability.
ro.root.aboutPage.responsibility.body: SDK’s role is to keep the engagement coherent as specialists contribute different parts of the work.
ro.root.aboutPage.facts.heading: A registered company, available through direct business channels.
ro.root.aboutPage.facts.name: Legal name
ro.root.aboutPage.cta.title: Bring the system, the constraint and the decision that needs ownership.
ro.root.aboutPage.cta.body: We will begin by determining what expertise the work requires and whether SDK is the right company to coordinate it.
ro.root.aboutPage.cta.label: Discuss a project
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.hero.title: Reduce uncertainty before it becomes delivery risk.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.hero.intro: SDK makes the problem, decisions, responsibilities and evidence visible throughout an engagement. The process adapts to the system, but the client always knows what is being decided and what comes next.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.heading: The first step depends on what you already know.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.intro: Starting implementation too early makes uncertainty expensive. Starting with another generic discovery exercise wastes time when the outcome is already clear.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.items[0].c: The system boundary, desired change and acceptance conditions are understood. We validate assumptions, compose the delivery team and plan the workstream.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.items[1].t: The problem is visible, but the path is not
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.items[1].c: The system is creating cost, risk or delay, but the cause or responsible response is unclear. We begin with a bounded technical assessment.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.heading: Four stages, each ending in a decision.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.intro: Progress is not measured by activity alone. Each stage produces evidence the client can review before more commitment is made.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].purp: Establish what the business needs, what the system does today and where uncertainty sits.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].acti: Inspect the relevant system and operating context
Define success, access and known unknowns
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].outp: A concise problem definition, current-state view and proposed scope.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].deci: Is there enough evidence to design the response?
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].purp: Turn the problem into technical options, delivery boundaries and explicit trade-offs.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].acti: Identify risks, dependencies and migration steps
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].outp: A technical approach, decision record, milestones and acceptance criteria.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].deci: Is this the right approach and commitment?
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].purp: Deliver the agreed change while keeping quality, risk and progress visible.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].acti: Record decisions, evidence and unresolved risks
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].outp: Working changes, review evidence and current operational documentation.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].deci: Does the increment meet its acceptance conditions?
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].purp: Place the system and the knowledge needed to operate it under client control.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].acti: Transfer context to the people retaining ownership
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].outp: Client-controlled code, infrastructure, documentation and agreed follow-up actions.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].deci: Can the client operate and evolve the delivered scope?
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.responsibility.headin: The team can change with the work. Responsibility does not disappear between specialists.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.responsibility.body: SDK selects independent specialists for the disciplines an engagement requires and coordinates them through one delivery framework. Decisions, access, documentation and work status are kept visible so knowledge does not remain with one individual.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.responsibility.items[: Defines the engagement framework, coordinates delivery and remains accountable for the quality controls agreed with the client.
Contribute the experience required by the system and work within shared decisions, review practices and acceptance criteria.
Provides business context, system access and timely decisions while retaining control of its repositories, infrastructure and information.
Keeps architecture decisions, risks, progress and operating knowledge accessible beyond any single contributor.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.heading: Confidence comes from mechanisms you can inspect.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.intro: We avoid unqualified promises such as secure, scalable or production-ready. The engagement defines how those qualities will be examined and evidenced for the system in question.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[0].copy: Material architecture and scope choices record the context, trade-offs and consequences instead of disappearing into meetings.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[1].copy: Work is divided into changes that can be inspected, tested and accepted before risk accumulates.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[2].copy: Tests, security checks, performance evidence and deployment controls are selected according to the actual failure risk.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[3].copy: Documentation, access, recovery steps and unresolved risks are treated as delivery work, not optional material after launch.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.scope.heading: Surface the change. Explain the consequence. Decide before proceeding.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.scope.body: Existing systems reveal information as they are inspected and changed. When an assumption fails or a new dependency appears, SDK records the evidence, explains its effect on scope, risk and sequence, and asks for a decision. The change does not disappear into an invoice or a delayed handover.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.scope.steps[1]: Explain the technical and commercial consequence
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.cta.title: Start with the uncertainty that is blocking the work.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.cta.body: Tell us what is known, what is under pressure and what decision your organization needs to make next.
ro.root.howWeWorkPage.cta.label: Discuss the situation
ro.root.servicesPage.hero.title: The problem defines the engineering team.
ro.root.servicesPage.hero.intro: SDK brings together the specialists a system actually requires, coordinates their work and remains accountable for delivery quality. Start with one technical decision or give us a defined workstream to own.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.heading: Start with the pressure on the system.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.intro: A useful engagement starts with the constraint, not a catalogue of technologies.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[0].cop: Reduce the risk and cost of changing software that can no longer keep accumulating patches.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[1].cop: Design and deliver backend platforms, integrations and product systems around a clear operating need.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[2].cop: Put AI into a real workflow with the data, evaluation and operational controls it needs.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[3].cop: Find the causes behind reliability, deployment, performance or data-flow problems.
ro.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[4].cop: Turn an unclear technical situation into evidence, options and a defensible next decision.
ro.root.servicesPage.capabilities.heading: Engineering depth, organized around the decision in front of you.
ro.root.servicesPage.capabilities.intro: Each capability can stand alone or combine with others when the system crosses boundaries.
Change an aging system without losing what still works.
The system matters to the business, but upgrades are risky, delivery is slowing down or too much knowledge sits in undocumented behavior.
Dependencies, runtime constraints and unsupported components
Data flows, integrations and hidden operational coupling
Change risk, test coverage and migration boundaries
Current-state assessment and prioritized modernization plan
Map what the system does today, where change is dangerous and which boundary can move first.
Build the parts of the product that carry the business rules.
A product needs APIs, integrations, authorization, asynchronous work or realtime behavior that must remain understandable as requirements change.
Domain boundaries, users and access rules
Integration contracts, failure modes and data ownership
Operational volume, latency and consistency requirements
Backend services, APIs and integration layers
Queues, events and realtime application flows
Define the business boundary, the data it owns and the failure conditions the design must tolerate.
Move AI from a convincing demo into an accountable workflow.
A manual process is expensive or slow, but an AI feature will only be useful if its inputs, outputs, evaluation and fallback behavior are controlled.
Workflow decisions that require a model and those that do not
Source data, permissions and retrieval quality
Evaluation criteria, human review and failure handling
LLM integrations, agents and workflow automation
Choose one workflow, define an acceptable result and measure the current human process before automating it.
Make production behavior visible before changing capacity.
Deployments are fragile, incidents are hard to explain, infrastructure costs are unclear or the system is approaching an operational limit.
Deployment path, environments and recovery procedures
Logs, metrics, traces and incident evidence
Resource constraints, bottlenecks and scaling assumptions
Establish what the system is doing under real load and how the team currently detects and recovers from failure.
Connect data, operations and the people using the system.
The product needs a dependable data path and an interface that makes complex operational work easier to understand and complete.
Data ownership, lifecycle, search and access patterns
User tasks, decision points and error recovery
Server and browser boundaries that affect performance
Data models, search, cache and ingestion flows
Operational web interfaces and internal tooling
Follow one critical user task from source data to final decision and identify where context is lost.
ro.root.servicesPage.engagements.heading: Match the commitment to what is already known.
ro.root.servicesPage.engagements.intro: An uncertain system needs evidence before a responsible implementation commitment. A defined outcome can move directly into a focused workstream.
ro.root.servicesPage.engagements.options[0]: A consequential decision where the current state, risk or implementation path is unclear.
Evidence, options, risks and a prioritized recommendation the client can use with or without SDK.
A bounded investigation with agreed access, questions and deliverables.
ro.root.servicesPage.engagements.options[1]: A defined technical outcome that needs a composed team and clear delivery ownership.
Working changes, reviewed decisions, deployment evidence and documentation for the agreed scope.
A focused delivery period with visible checkpoints and acceptance criteria.
ro.root.servicesPage.engagements.options[2]: A system that needs staged modernization or continued ownership of a technical workstream.
A maintained roadmap, incremental delivery and an operating record of decisions, risks and progress.
A continuing engagement reviewed against an agreed workstream and priorities.
ro.root.servicesPage.teamModel.heading: Specialists selected for the system. One company accountable to the client.
ro.root.servicesPage.teamModel.body: SDK works with independent engineering specialists. We compose the team around the problem, coordinate the work and set the quality framework for the engagement. The client does not need to recruit, align and manage a collection of unrelated contributors.
ro.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[0].cop: Clarify the system, constraints, decisions and outcome before deciding who should do the work.
ro.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[1].cop: Select the disciplines and experience relevant to the engagement instead of forcing it into a fixed bench.
ro.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[2].cop: Use visible decisions, reviews, acceptance criteria and operational evidence throughout delivery.
ro.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[3].cop: Keep code, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge in the client’s control.
ro.root.servicesPage.cta.title: You do not need to arrive with a finished specification.
ro.root.servicesPage.cta.body: Describe the system, the pressure on it and the decision you need to make. We will start by determining whether SDK is a useful fit.
ro.root.servicesPage.cta.label: Discuss the problem
ro.root.workPage.hero.eyebrow: Problems we are set up to solve
ro.root.workPage.hero.title: Look at the engineering problem before prescribing the project.
ro.root.workPage.hero.intro: The scenarios below show how SDK approaches technically consequential situations. They describe capabilities and decision paths, not invented client case studies or unsupported results.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.heading: Recognize the pressure. Then find the responsible first move.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.intro: A useful response connects business exposure to technical evidence and a decision the organization can act on.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[0].title: The system is too important to replace blindly—and too costly to leave alone.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[0].situati: Delivery slows as dependencies age, knowledge narrows and every change reaches further than expected.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[0].questio: What must remain available during change?
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].title: The platform is under pressure, but capacity may not be the real problem.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].situati: Latency, incidents or infrastructure cost are increasing and the available signals do not explain why.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].signals: Recovery depends on a few people
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].questio: Where does time and capacity go?
What evidence is missing during incidents?
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[2].title: The AI demo works. The operating model around it does not exist yet.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[2].situati: A promising model interaction must become a controlled workflow with trusted data, evaluation and human responsibility.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[2].questio: How will quality be measured over time?
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].title: The product needs focused engineering ownership for a critical phase.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].situati: The internal team has a defined priority but lacks one or more disciplines needed to carry the workstream safely.
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].signals: A critical roadmap item remains blocked
ro.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].questio: Where do client decisions remain essential?
ro.root.workPage.principle.heading: A portfolio is only persuasive when the evidence is real.
ro.root.workPage.principle.body: SDK will publish named clients, quantified outcomes and testimonials only when the work, result and permission can be verified. Until then, this page shows the situations we are equipped to investigate and the deliverables that move them forward.
ro.root.workPage.fit.heading: The strongest work starts with access, responsibility and a real decision to make.
ro.root.workPage.fit.intro: Technical difficulty is welcome. An engagement becomes ineffective when the organization cannot provide context, access or decision ownership.
ro.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[0]: A material software, data, AI or infrastructure constraint
ro.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[1]: Access to the system and people who understand its current state
ro.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[2]: A decision-maker who can resolve scope and trade-offs
ro.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[3]: Willingness to examine evidence before committing to a solution
ro.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[0]: Anonymous ticket capacity with no owned outcome
ro.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[1]: A request to validate a predetermined answer regardless of evidence
ro.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[2]: No practical access to the relevant system or stakeholders
ro.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[3]: Selection based only on the lowest individual day rate
ro.root.workPage.cta.title: Start with what the system is costing, delaying or putting at risk.
ro.root.workPage.cta.body: You do not need to diagnose it before contacting SDK. Tell us what is happening and which decision is currently blocked.
ro.root.workPage.cta.label: Discuss the situation

bg.root.designSystem.title: The shared visual foundation for the website and client portal.
bg.root.designSystem.intro: This page renders every token, primitive and state defined in docs/design/design-system.md and docs/design/patterns.md. It is the reference during development. It is intentionally not linked from production navigation.
bg.root.designSystem.colors.title: A small palette, used with intent.
bg.root.designSystem.colors.intro: Brand green is for actions and meaningful highlights only — never decoration. Green backgrounds always carry dark text; green text only appears on dark surfaces.
bg.root.designSystem.type.title: JetBrains Mono, tuned like an editorial type system.
bg.root.designSystem.type.intro: Headlines set tight and large; labels set small, uppercase and tracked. Body copy never goes below 14px.
bg.root.designSystem.components.title: Restrained primitives, aligned to the reference.
bg.root.designSystem.components.intro: Buttons, badges, cards and links. One radius family, 1px borders, and no decoration beyond what the approved designs use.
bg.root.designSystem.states.title: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
bg.root.designSystem.states.intro: No color inventions. Skeleton uses the line tone, empty states a dashed border, errors stay on the paper surface with strong dark emphasis.
bg.root.designSystem.states.loading: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
bg.root.designSystem.states.whenProjectExis: When a project or request exists, it will appear here.
bg.root.designSystem.states.tryAgain: Try again, or contact support if the problem persists.
bg.root.designSystem.darkSurface.title: Dark sections carry the same system.
bg.root.designSystem.darkSurface.intro: Primary text turns light, secondary turns fog, and green is used for highlights. Border line darkens to keep the composition quiet.
bg.root.designSystem.brandSurface.title: One brand section per page, at most.
bg.root.designSystem.brandSurface.intro: Green backgrounds carry dark text. Use this sparingly — it is the loudest surface in the system.
bg.root.enquiry.title: Start a project
bg.root.enquiry.subtitle: Tell us what you are trying to build, modernize, automate or fix. A useful enquiry starts with the pressure on the system and the decision you need to make.
bg.root.enquiry.body: The form collects the minimum information needed to respond thoughtfully. Nothing is shared outside SDK Enterprises, and you can also reach us directly at hello@sdk.enterprises.
bg.root.enquiry.body2: Your technical and commercial context stays together while SDK assesses whether the work is a fit.
bg.root.enquiry.heroSignals[0]: A finished specification is not required
bg.root.enquiry.heroSignals[1]: Technical and commercial context stays together
bg.root.enquiry.reasonsHeading: Bring the pressure on the system, not a polished procurement document.
bg.root.enquiry.reasonsIntro: The form is designed to establish whether SDK can make the next technical decision easier.
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[0].title: A system needs to change
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[0].copy: Modernization, migration or integration work is blocked by uncertainty in the current state.
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[1].title: A platform is under pressure
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[1].copy: Reliability, delivery speed, infrastructure or data behavior has become a business constraint.
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[2].title: An AI workflow needs engineering controls
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[2].copy: The use case is promising, but data, evaluation, review or operation is not yet defined.
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[3].title: A workstream needs the right specialists
bg.root.enquiry.reasons[3].copy: The outcome is clear, but the project crosses disciplines the current team cannot cover alone.
bg.root.enquiry.formHeading: Give us enough information to respond usefully.
bg.root.enquiry.formIntro: Explain what is happening, why it matters and what has already been tried. Unknown budget, timing or technical details can remain marked as such.
bg.root.enquiry.nextStepsBody: After you submit the form, we read it ourselves. If it is a fit, we will reply with a short written assessment and a proposed engagement model. If it is not a fit, we will tell you why and suggest an alternative.
bg.root.enquiry.nextStep1Body: We review the system, constraint and requested outcome against SDK's current capacity and relevant expertise.
bg.root.enquiry.nextStep2Body: A short written response: what we think the problem is, whether it is a fit, and what the first move would be.
bg.root.enquiry.nextStep3Body: A 30-minute call or an async exchange to clarify scope, constraints, and timeline. No pitch deck unless you want one.
bg.root.enquiry.nextStep4Body: A written proposal with scope, fixed price or rate, timeline, and milestones. You sign, we start.
bg.root.enquiry.validation.descriptionTooSh: Description must be at least 50 characters
bg.root.enquiry.validation.contextTooLong: Supporting context must be under 4000 characters
bg.root.enquiry.success.title: Enquiry sent
bg.root.enquiry.success.body: Thanks — we'll review the project context and reply with the next useful question or an assessment of fit.
bg.root.enquiry.error.title: Something went wrong
bg.root.enquiry.error.body: We couldn't send your enquiry. Please try again or email us directly.
bg.root.homePage.hero.eyebrow: Software · AI · Cloud · Data · Systems Engineering
bg.root.homePage.hero.title: Bring the system that needs a responsible way forward.
bg.root.homePage.hero.intro: SDK Enterprises assembles the engineering specialists a project actually requires, coordinates their work and remains accountable for the quality framework presented to the client. We help organizations diagnose, modernize, build and operate technically consequential software.
bg.root.homePage.opening.heading: A technology list cannot tell you what the project needs.
bg.root.homePage.opening.body: A modernization programme, an AI workflow and a platform reliability problem may touch similar technologies while requiring completely different decisions, disciplines and delivery controls. SDK starts with the pressure on the system and the outcome the organization needs to own.
bg.root.homePage.opening.body2: That may lead to a bounded technical assessment, a focused engineering workstream or a continuing technical partnership. The commitment should match what is already known—not conceal uncertainty inside a larger proposal.
bg.root.homePage.opening.principles[0].copy: When the current state or implementation path is unclear, establish the evidence needed for a responsible decision first.
bg.root.homePage.opening.principles[1].copy: Select the disciplines the system requires instead of forcing every engagement into the same available team.
bg.root.homePage.opening.principles[2].copy: Keep decisions, repositories, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge under client control.
bg.root.homePage.system.heading: The work rarely stops at the boundary of one technology.
bg.root.homePage.system.intro: SDK can focus on one layer or coordinate a workstream that crosses several. The map below shows the engineering concerns that often need to be considered together.
bg.root.homePage.system.items[0].title: Workflow and interface
bg.root.homePage.system.items[0].copy: The user task, operational decision and recovery path the software must make understandable.
bg.root.homePage.system.items[1].title: Business platform
bg.root.homePage.system.items[1].copy: The services, APIs, permissions and integration contracts that carry the organization’s rules.
bg.root.homePage.system.items[2].title: AI and automation
bg.root.homePage.system.items[2].copy: The model-assisted decisions, retrieval, evaluation and human review controls inside a real workflow.
bg.root.homePage.system.items[3].title: Data and state
bg.root.homePage.system.items[3].copy: The ownership, consistency, search, cache and lifecycle rules behind system behavior.
bg.root.homePage.system.items[4].title: Production operation
bg.root.homePage.system.items[4].copy: The deployment, observability, recovery and infrastructure mechanisms needed to operate the system.
bg.root.homePage.scenarios.heading: Technical work becomes urgent through its effect on the business.
bg.root.homePage.scenarios.intro: The following scenarios are capability examples, not invented client case studies. They show how SDK connects symptoms to questions and tangible next deliverables.
bg.root.homePage.companyModel.heading: A project-specific team without transferring coordination risk to the client.
bg.root.homePage.companyModel.intro: SDK works with independent engineering specialists. The disciplines can change with the work, while the client retains one company relationship and one delivery framework.
bg.root.homePage.engagements.eyebrow: Choose the right level of commitment
bg.root.homePage.engagements.heading: Do not buy implementation before the system can support an implementation decision.
bg.root.homePage.engagements.intro: Start with evidence when uncertainty is material. Move directly into delivery when the outcome, boundary and acceptance conditions are already understood.
bg.root.homePage.process.heading: Every stage should end with evidence and a decision.
bg.root.homePage.process.intro: Activity alone does not show that a project is progressing. SDK structures the engagement so the client can review what has been learned, built and transferred before making the next commitment.
bg.root.homePage.quality.heading: Confidence should come from visible mechanisms, not adjectives.
bg.root.homePage.quality.intro: Terms such as secure, scalable and production-ready only become meaningful when the engagement defines how they will be examined for the actual system and risk.
bg.root.homePage.fit.heading: The engagement needs a real constraint, system access and someone able to decide.
bg.root.homePage.fit.intro: SDK is designed for owned technical outcomes. It is not a marketplace for anonymous ticket capacity or a way to validate a predetermined answer without examining the evidence.
bg.root.homePage.cta.title: You do not need to turn the problem into a polished specification first.
bg.root.homePage.cta.body: Tell us what the system is doing, what it is costing or delaying, and which decision is currently blocked. SDK will begin by determining whether the work is a fit and what the first useful move should be.
bg.root.homePage.cta.label: Discuss the situation

bg.root.aboutPage.hero.title: A company built to compose the right engineering capability for the work.
bg.root.aboutPage.hero.intro: SDK engages independent engineering specialists according to the system and remains responsible for the delivery framework and quality expectations presented to the client.
bg.root.aboutPage.model.heading: The available bench does not decide what your system receives.
bg.root.aboutPage.model.intro: A fixed internal team can be efficient when every project needs the same disciplines. Complex systems often do not. SDK starts with the problem, determines which engineering capability is relevant and brings the required independent specialists into one engagement.
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[0].title: One client relationship
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[0].copy: The client engages SDK Enterprises. SDK provides the delivery framework instead of leaving the client to coordinate unrelated individual suppliers.
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[1].title: A composed team
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[1].copy: The disciplines involved can change with the stage of work, from assessment and architecture to implementation and operation.
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[2].title: Shared quality expectations
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[2].copy: The engagement defines review practices, acceptance evidence, decision records and handover requirements appropriate to its risks.
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[3].title: Client control
bg.root.aboutPage.model.items[3].copy: Repositories, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge are organized to remain under the client’s control.
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.heading: Relevant experience matters more than adding another profile to the project.
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.body: SDK considers the system, delivery stage, technical risk and collaboration needs before composing a team. The public site will not claim a network size, acceptance rate or universal seniority standard without a documented basis.
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[0].title: Problem relevance
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[0].copy: Experience is considered against the actual system boundary and technical decisions, not only a list of technologies.
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[1].title: Delivery responsibility
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[1].copy: Specialists need to work within visible decisions, review expectations and client-owned environments.
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[2].title: Collaboration fit
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[2].copy: The ability to explain trade-offs and work with client stakeholders is part of successful technical delivery.
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[3].title: Continuity
bg.root.aboutPage.selection.items[3].copy: Important context is recorded so ownership does not depend on one contributor remaining indefinitely.
bg.root.aboutPage.responsibility.heading: Flexible team composition should not create ambiguous accountability.
bg.root.aboutPage.responsibility.body: SDK’s role is to keep the engagement coherent as specialists contribute different parts of the work.
bg.root.aboutPage.facts.heading: A registered company, available through direct business channels.
bg.root.aboutPage.facts.name: Legal name
bg.root.aboutPage.cta.title: Bring the system, the constraint and the decision that needs ownership.
bg.root.aboutPage.cta.body: We will begin by determining what expertise the work requires and whether SDK is the right company to coordinate it.
bg.root.aboutPage.cta.label: Discuss a project
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.hero.title: Reduce uncertainty before it becomes delivery risk.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.hero.intro: SDK makes the problem, decisions, responsibilities and evidence visible throughout an engagement. The process adapts to the system, but the client always knows what is being decided and what comes next.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.heading: The first step depends on what you already know.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.intro: Starting implementation too early makes uncertainty expensive. Starting with another generic discovery exercise wastes time when the outcome is already clear.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.items[0].c: The system boundary, desired change and acceptance conditions are understood. We validate assumptions, compose the delivery team and plan the workstream.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.items[1].t: The problem is visible, but the path is not
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.entryPaths.items[1].c: The system is creating cost, risk or delay, but the cause or responsible response is unclear. We begin with a bounded technical assessment.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.heading: Four stages, each ending in a decision.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.intro: Progress is not measured by activity alone. Each stage produces evidence the client can review before more commitment is made.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].purp: Establish what the business needs, what the system does today and where uncertainty sits.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].acti: Inspect the relevant system and operating context
Define success, access and known unknowns
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].outp: A concise problem definition, current-state view and proposed scope.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[0].deci: Is there enough evidence to design the response?
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].purp: Turn the problem into technical options, delivery boundaries and explicit trade-offs.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].acti: Identify risks, dependencies and migration steps
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].outp: A technical approach, decision record, milestones and acceptance criteria.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[1].deci: Is this the right approach and commitment?
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].purp: Deliver the agreed change while keeping quality, risk and progress visible.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].acti: Record decisions, evidence and unresolved risks
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].outp: Working changes, review evidence and current operational documentation.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[2].deci: Does the increment meet its acceptance conditions?
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].purp: Place the system and the knowledge needed to operate it under client control.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].acti: Transfer context to the people retaining ownership
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].outp: Client-controlled code, infrastructure, documentation and agreed follow-up actions.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.process.items[3].deci: Can the client operate and evolve the delivered scope?
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.responsibility.headin: The team can change with the work. Responsibility does not disappear between specialists.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.responsibility.body: SDK selects independent specialists for the disciplines an engagement requires and coordinates them through one delivery framework. Decisions, access, documentation and work status are kept visible so knowledge does not remain with one individual.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.responsibility.items[: Defines the engagement framework, coordinates delivery and remains accountable for the quality controls agreed with the client.
Contribute the experience required by the system and work within shared decisions, review practices and acceptance criteria.
Provides business context, system access and timely decisions while retaining control of its repositories, infrastructure and information.
Keeps architecture decisions, risks, progress and operating knowledge accessible beyond any single contributor.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.heading: Confidence comes from mechanisms you can inspect.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.intro: We avoid unqualified promises such as secure, scalable or production-ready. The engagement defines how those qualities will be examined and evidenced for the system in question.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[0].copy: Material architecture and scope choices record the context, trade-offs and consequences instead of disappearing into meetings.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[1].copy: Work is divided into changes that can be inspected, tested and accepted before risk accumulates.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[2].copy: Tests, security checks, performance evidence and deployment controls are selected according to the actual failure risk.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.quality.items[3].copy: Documentation, access, recovery steps and unresolved risks are treated as delivery work, not optional material after launch.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.scope.heading: Surface the change. Explain the consequence. Decide before proceeding.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.scope.body: Existing systems reveal information as they are inspected and changed. When an assumption fails or a new dependency appears, SDK records the evidence, explains its effect on scope, risk and sequence, and asks for a decision. The change does not disappear into an invoice or a delayed handover.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.scope.steps[1]: Explain the technical and commercial consequence
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.cta.title: Start with the uncertainty that is blocking the work.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.cta.body: Tell us what is known, what is under pressure and what decision your organization needs to make next.
bg.root.howWeWorkPage.cta.label: Discuss the situation
bg.root.servicesPage.hero.title: The problem defines the engineering team.
bg.root.servicesPage.hero.intro: SDK brings together the specialists a system actually requires, coordinates their work and remains accountable for delivery quality. Start with one technical decision or give us a defined workstream to own.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.heading: Start with the pressure on the system.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.intro: A useful engagement starts with the constraint, not a catalogue of technologies.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[0].cop: Reduce the risk and cost of changing software that can no longer keep accumulating patches.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[1].cop: Design and deliver backend platforms, integrations and product systems around a clear operating need.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[2].cop: Put AI into a real workflow with the data, evaluation and operational controls it needs.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[3].cop: Find the causes behind reliability, deployment, performance or data-flow problems.
bg.root.servicesPage.navigator.items[4].cop: Turn an unclear technical situation into evidence, options and a defensible next decision.
bg.root.servicesPage.capabilities.heading: Engineering depth, organized around the decision in front of you.
bg.root.servicesPage.capabilities.intro: Each capability can stand alone or combine with others when the system crosses boundaries.
Change an aging system without losing what still works.
The system matters to the business, but upgrades are risky, delivery is slowing down or too much knowledge sits in undocumented behavior.
Dependencies, runtime constraints and unsupported components
Data flows, integrations and hidden operational coupling
Change risk, test coverage and migration boundaries
Current-state assessment and prioritized modernization plan
Map what the system does today, where change is dangerous and which boundary can move first.
Build the parts of the product that carry the business rules.
A product needs APIs, integrations, authorization, asynchronous work or realtime behavior that must remain understandable as requirements change.
Domain boundaries, users and access rules
Integration contracts, failure modes and data ownership
Operational volume, latency and consistency requirements
Backend services, APIs and integration layers
Queues, events and realtime application flows
Define the business boundary, the data it owns and the failure conditions the design must tolerate.
Move AI from a convincing demo into an accountable workflow.
A manual process is expensive or slow, but an AI feature will only be useful if its inputs, outputs, evaluation and fallback behavior are controlled.
Workflow decisions that require a model and those that do not
Source data, permissions and retrieval quality
Evaluation criteria, human review and failure handling
LLM integrations, agents and workflow automation
Choose one workflow, define an acceptable result and measure the current human process before automating it.
Make production behavior visible before changing capacity.
Deployments are fragile, incidents are hard to explain, infrastructure costs are unclear or the system is approaching an operational limit.
Deployment path, environments and recovery procedures
Logs, metrics, traces and incident evidence
Resource constraints, bottlenecks and scaling assumptions
Establish what the system is doing under real load and how the team currently detects and recovers from failure.
Connect data, operations and the people using the system.
The product needs a dependable data path and an interface that makes complex operational work easier to understand and complete.
Data ownership, lifecycle, search and access patterns
User tasks, decision points and error recovery
Server and browser boundaries that affect performance
Data models, search, cache and ingestion flows
Operational web interfaces and internal tooling
Follow one critical user task from source data to final decision and identify where context is lost.
bg.root.servicesPage.engagements.heading: Match the commitment to what is already known.
bg.root.servicesPage.engagements.intro: An uncertain system needs evidence before a responsible implementation commitment. A defined outcome can move directly into a focused workstream.
bg.root.servicesPage.engagements.options[0]: A consequential decision where the current state, risk or implementation path is unclear.
Evidence, options, risks and a prioritized recommendation the client can use with or without SDK.
A bounded investigation with agreed access, questions and deliverables.
bg.root.servicesPage.engagements.options[1]: A defined technical outcome that needs a composed team and clear delivery ownership.
Working changes, reviewed decisions, deployment evidence and documentation for the agreed scope.
A focused delivery period with visible checkpoints and acceptance criteria.
bg.root.servicesPage.engagements.options[2]: A system that needs staged modernization or continued ownership of a technical workstream.
A maintained roadmap, incremental delivery and an operating record of decisions, risks and progress.
A continuing engagement reviewed against an agreed workstream and priorities.
bg.root.servicesPage.teamModel.heading: Specialists selected for the system. One company accountable to the client.
bg.root.servicesPage.teamModel.body: SDK works with independent engineering specialists. We compose the team around the problem, coordinate the work and set the quality framework for the engagement. The client does not need to recruit, align and manage a collection of unrelated contributors.
bg.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[0].cop: Clarify the system, constraints, decisions and outcome before deciding who should do the work.
bg.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[1].cop: Select the disciplines and experience relevant to the engagement instead of forcing it into a fixed bench.
bg.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[2].cop: Use visible decisions, reviews, acceptance criteria and operational evidence throughout delivery.
bg.root.servicesPage.teamModel.steps[3].cop: Keep code, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge in the client’s control.
bg.root.servicesPage.cta.title: You do not need to arrive with a finished specification.
bg.root.servicesPage.cta.body: Describe the system, the pressure on it and the decision you need to make. We will start by determining whether SDK is a useful fit.
bg.root.servicesPage.cta.label: Discuss the problem
bg.root.workPage.hero.eyebrow: Problems we are set up to solve
bg.root.workPage.hero.title: Look at the engineering problem before prescribing the project.
bg.root.workPage.hero.intro: The scenarios below show how SDK approaches technically consequential situations. They describe capabilities and decision paths, not invented client case studies or unsupported results.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.heading: Recognize the pressure. Then find the responsible first move.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.intro: A useful response connects business exposure to technical evidence and a decision the organization can act on.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[0].title: The system is too important to replace blindly—and too costly to leave alone.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[0].situati: Delivery slows as dependencies age, knowledge narrows and every change reaches further than expected.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[0].questio: What must remain available during change?
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].title: The platform is under pressure, but capacity may not be the real problem.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].situati: Latency, incidents or infrastructure cost are increasing and the available signals do not explain why.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].signals: Recovery depends on a few people
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[1].questio: Where does time and capacity go?
What evidence is missing during incidents?
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[2].title: The AI demo works. The operating model around it does not exist yet.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[2].situati: A promising model interaction must become a controlled workflow with trusted data, evaluation and human responsibility.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[2].questio: How will quality be measured over time?
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].title: The product needs focused engineering ownership for a critical phase.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].situati: The internal team has a defined priority but lacks one or more disciplines needed to carry the workstream safely.
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].signals: A critical roadmap item remains blocked
bg.root.workPage.scenarios.items[3].questio: Where do client decisions remain essential?
bg.root.workPage.principle.heading: A portfolio is only persuasive when the evidence is real.
bg.root.workPage.principle.body: SDK will publish named clients, quantified outcomes and testimonials only when the work, result and permission can be verified. Until then, this page shows the situations we are equipped to investigate and the deliverables that move them forward.
bg.root.workPage.fit.heading: The strongest work starts with access, responsibility and a real decision to make.
bg.root.workPage.fit.intro: Technical difficulty is welcome. An engagement becomes ineffective when the organization cannot provide context, access or decision ownership.
bg.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[0]: A material software, data, AI or infrastructure constraint
bg.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[1]: Access to the system and people who understand its current state
bg.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[2]: A decision-maker who can resolve scope and trade-offs
bg.root.workPage.fit.fitItems[3]: Willingness to examine evidence before committing to a solution
bg.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[0]: Anonymous ticket capacity with no owned outcome
bg.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[1]: A request to validate a predetermined answer regardless of evidence
bg.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[2]: No practical access to the relevant system or stakeholders
bg.root.workPage.fit.notFitItems[3]: Selection based only on the lowest individual day rate
bg.root.workPage.cta.title: Start with what the system is costing, delaying or putting at risk.
bg.root.workPage.cta.body: You do not need to diagnose it before contacting SDK. Tell us what is happening and which decision is currently blocked.
bg.root.workPage.cta.label: Discuss the situation

el.root.designSystem.title: The shared visual foundation for the website and client portal.
el.root.designSystem.intro: This page renders every token, primitive and state defined in docs/design/design-system.md and docs/design/patterns.md. It is the reference during development. It is intentionally not linked from production navigation.
el.root.designSystem.colors.title: A small palette, used with intent.
el.root.designSystem.colors.intro: Brand green is for actions and meaningful highlights only — never decoration. Green backgrounds always carry dark text; green text only appears on dark surfaces.
el.root.designSystem.type.title: JetBrains Mono, tuned like an editorial type system.
el.root.designSystem.type.intro: Headlines set tight and large; labels set small, uppercase and tracked. Body copy never goes below 14px.
el.root.designSystem.components.title: Restrained primitives, aligned to the reference.
el.root.designSystem.components.intro: Buttons, badges, cards and links. One radius family, 1px borders, and no decoration beyond what the approved designs use.
el.root.designSystem.states.title: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
el.root.designSystem.states.intro: No color inventions. Skeleton uses the line tone, empty states a dashed border, errors stay on the paper surface with strong dark emphasis.
el.root.designSystem.states.loading: Loading, empty and error — consistent surfaces.
el.root.designSystem.states.whenProjectExis: When a project or request exists, it will appear here.
el.root.designSystem.states.tryAgain: Try again, or contact support if the problem persists.
el.root.designSystem.darkSurface.title: Dark sections carry the same system.
el.root.designSystem.darkSurface.intro: Primary text turns light, secondary turns fog, and green is used for highlights. Border line darkens to keep the composition quiet.
el.root.designSystem.brandSurface.title: One brand section per page, at most.
el.root.designSystem.brandSurface.intro: Green backgrounds carry dark text. Use this sparingly — it is the loudest surface in the system.
el.root.enquiry.title: Start a project
el.root.enquiry.subtitle: Tell us what you are trying to build, modernize, automate or fix. A useful enquiry starts with the pressure on the system and the decision you need to make.
el.root.enquiry.body: The form collects the minimum information needed to respond thoughtfully. Nothing is shared outside SDK Enterprises, and you can also reach us directly at hello@sdk.enterprises.
el.root.enquiry.body2: Your technical and commercial context stays together while SDK assesses whether the work is a fit.
el.root.enquiry.heroSignals[0]: A finished specification is not required
el.root.enquiry.heroSignals[1]: Technical and commercial context stays together
el.root.enquiry.reasonsHeading: Bring the pressure on the system, not a polished procurement document.
el.root.enquiry.reasonsIntro: The form is designed to establish whether SDK can make the next technical decision easier.
el.root.enquiry.reasons[0].title: A system needs to change
el.root.enquiry.reasons[0].copy: Modernization, migration or integration work is blocked by uncertainty in the current state.
el.root.enquiry.reasons[1].title: A platform is under pressure
el.root.enquiry.reasons[1].copy: Reliability, delivery speed, infrastructure or data behavior has become a business constraint.
el.root.enquiry.reasons[2].title: An AI workflow needs engineering controls
el.root.enquiry.reasons[2].copy: The use case is promising, but data, evaluation, review or operation is not yet defined.
el.root.enquiry.reasons[3].title: A workstream needs the right specialists
el.root.enquiry.reasons[3].copy: The outcome is clear, but the project crosses disciplines the current team cannot cover alone.
el.root.enquiry.formHeading: Give us enough information to respond usefully.
el.root.enquiry.formIntro: Explain what is happening, why it matters and what has already been tried. Unknown budget, timing or technical details can remain marked as such.
el.root.enquiry.nextStepsBody: After you submit the form, we read it ourselves. If it is a fit, we will reply with a short written assessment and a proposed engagement model. If it is not a fit, we will tell you why and suggest an alternative.
el.root.enquiry.nextStep1Body: We review the system, constraint and requested outcome against SDK's current capacity and relevant expertise.
el.root.enquiry.nextStep2Body: A short written response: what we think the problem is, whether it is a fit, and what the first move would be.
el.root.enquiry.nextStep3Body: A 30-minute call or an async exchange to clarify scope, constraints, and timeline. No pitch deck unless you want one.
el.root.enquiry.nextStep4Body: A written proposal with scope, fixed price or rate, timeline, and milestones. You sign, we start.
el.root.enquiry.validation.descriptionTooSh: Description must be at least 50 characters
el.root.enquiry.validation.contextTooLong: Supporting context must be under 4000 characters
el.root.enquiry.success.title: Enquiry sent
el.root.enquiry.success.body: Thanks — we'll review the project context and reply with the next useful question or an assessment of fit.
el.root.enquiry.error.title: Something went wrong
el.root.enquiry.error.body: We couldn't send your enquiry. Please try again or email us directly.
el.root.homePage.hero.eyebrow: Software · AI · Cloud · Data · Systems Engineering
el.root.homePage.hero.title: Bring the system that needs a responsible way forward.
el.root.homePage.hero.intro: SDK Enterprises assembles the engineering specialists a project actually requires, coordinates their work and remains accountable for the quality framework presented to the client. We help organizations diagnose, modernize, build and operate technically consequential software.
el.root.homePage.opening.heading: A technology list cannot tell you what the project needs.
el.root.homePage.opening.body: A modernization programme, an AI workflow and a platform reliability problem may touch similar technologies while requiring completely different decisions, disciplines and delivery controls. SDK starts with the pressure on the system and the outcome the organization needs to own.
el.root.homePage.opening.body2: That may lead to a bounded technical assessment, a focused engineering workstream or a continuing technical partnership. The commitment should match what is already known—not conceal uncertainty inside a larger proposal.
el.root.homePage.opening.principles[0].copy: When the current state or implementation path is unclear, establish the evidence needed for a responsible decision first.
el.root.homePage.opening.principles[1].copy: Select the disciplines the system requires instead of forcing every engagement into the same available team.
el.root.homePage.opening.principles[2].copy: Keep decisions, repositories, infrastructure, documentation and operating knowledge under client control.
el.root.homePage.system.heading: The work rarely stops at the boundary of one technology.
el.root.homePage.system.intro: SDK can focus on one layer or coordinate a workstream that crosses several. The map below shows the engineering concerns that often need to be considered together.
el.root.homePage.system.items[0].title: Workflow and interface
el.root.homePage.system.items[0].copy: The user task, operational decision and recovery path the software must make understandable.
el.root.homePage.system.items[1].title: Business platform
el.root.homePage.system.items[1].copy: The services, APIs, permissions and integration contracts that carry the organization’s rules.
el.root.homePage.system.items[2].title: AI and automation
el.root.homePage.system.items[2].copy: The model-assisted decisions, retrieval, evaluation and human review controls inside a real workflow.
el.root.homePage.system.items[3].title: Data and state
el.root.homePage.system.items[3].copy: The ownership, consistency, search, cache and lifecycle rules behind system behavior.
el.root.homePage.system.items[4].title: Production operation
el.root.homePage.system.items[4].copy: The deployment, observability, recovery and infrastructure mechanisms needed to operate the system.
el.root.homePage.scenarios.heading: Technical work becomes urgent through its effect on the business.
el.root.homePage.scenarios.intro: The following scenarios are capability examples, not invented client case studies. They show how SDK connects symptoms to questions and tangible next deliverables.
el.root.homePage.companyModel.heading: A project-specific team without transferring coordination risk to the client.
el.root.homePage.companyModel.intro: SDK works with independent engineering specialists. The disciplines can change with the work, while the client retains one company relationship and one delivery framework.
el.root.homePage.engagements.eyebrow: Choose the right level of commitment
el.root.homePage.engagements.heading: Do not buy implementation before the system can support an implementation decision.
el.root.homePage.engagements.intro: Start with evidence when uncertainty is material. Move directly into delivery when the outcome, boundary and acceptance conditions are already understood.
el.root.homePage.process.heading: Every stage should end with evidence and a decision.
el.root.homePage.process.intro: Activity alone does not show that a project is progressing. SDK structures the engagement so the client can review what has been learned, built and transferred before making the next commitment.
el.root.homePage.quality.heading: Confidence should come from visible mechanisms, not adjectives.
el.root.homePage.quality.intro: Terms such as secure, scalable and production-ready only become meaningful when the engagement defines how they will be examined for the actual system and risk.
el.root.homePage.fit.heading: The engagement needs a real constraint, system access and someone able to decide.
el.root.homePage.fit.intro: SDK is designed for owned technical outcomes. It is not a marketplace for anonymous ticket capacity or a way to validate a predetermined answer without examining the evidence.
el.root.homePage.cta.title: You do not need to turn the problem into a polished specification first.
el.root.homePage.cta.body: Tell us what the system is doing, what it is costing or delaying, and which decision is currently blocked. SDK will begin by determining whether the work is a fit and what the first useful move should be.
el.root.homePage.cta.label: Discuss the situation
